**US-01 (MVP, FR-CAT-001):** As a visitor I can filter published activities by destination, date and type so I can assess a relevant offer. Given a published occurrence with a future registration window, when I search the destination, then its detail shows dates, time zone, price unit, opening time and “not yet open”, without an enabled registration action. An empty result provides filter reset; an unavailable API presents an actionable retry without inventing inventory. Keyboard and Persian tasks follow the same route.

**US-02 (MVP, FR-TOUR-001):** As a customer I need to understand what a departure includes before paying. Given an approved published departure, when I open its itinerary, then each stop, transport leg, included and excluded meal and customer price is visible, but confidential supplier costs and internal notes are absent from page source, API and export. Given a material published change, agency assesses existing bookings and records customer notification; no silent contract change is assumed.

**US-03 (MVP, FR-EVT-001 / FR-ACA-001):** As a customer I can register only during the occurrence’s own window and only if seats remain. **TC-REG-001:** Given a published eligible occurrence, when server time equals open, then a hold may be created; when server time equals close, it is denied. Client clock and disabled buttons are not authoritative. **TC-REG-002:** Given one seat and two concurrent eligible requests, when both submit, then only one hold commits and the other receives sold-out feedback. A course and two cohorts can show one open and one closed independently.

**US-04 (MVP, FR-COM-001 / FR-PAY-001):** As a signed-in purchaser I can review the final price, go to an eligible gateway, and see a truthful outcome. Given a hold, when the user starts payment, show its deadline and displayed currency unit; never request card details in the site. Given independent local verification with matching amount and currency completed at or before the deadline, when the hold is unreleased, consume it once and create a paid-pending-confirmation booking without requiring provider paid-at. Given verification completed after the deadline, require both trustworthy provider paid-at at or before the deadline and an unreleased allocation; then consume once even if confirmation occurs after close. At the deadline, block new payment initiation and public admission; serialize consume versus release. A payment redirect by itself does not confirm booking. Duplicate callback has no second effect (TC-PAY-001).

**US-05 (MVP, FR-FIN-001):** As support I need to handle an unverified or late paid booking safely. Given a released hold and a subsequently verified payment, when reconciliation processes it, the expired booking moves to exception and payment remains verified; no inventory is reclaimed automatically, staff receives an exception and the customer sees “payment under review”. Refund is independently requested, approved and tracked. A deadline-passed allocation remains allocated until the serialized consume/release race decides it; if verification is late and paid-at is unavailable or untrustworthy, route to manual review. One local transaction never crosses a gateway network call. Waitlist after close requires an audited admin exception and available capacity.

**US-06 (MVP, FR-COM-001):** Given a souvenir in cart, when a user adds a tour, then explain incompatible cart types and offer separate purchase without silently discarding items. A homogeneous group of the same departure may use one quantity subject to capacity; differing departure inventory is not mixed.

**US-07 (MVP, FR-PART-001 / FR-TOUR-001):** As approved leader staff I can draft several tours and dated departures for my organization, submit them, and view agency feedback. Given another organization’s identifier, when I request its proposal via UI, API or export, then access is denied and no sensitive record is returned (TC-AUTH-001). Agency reviewers see submitted material and record approve/revise decision with actor/time. A role alone does not grant access to every organization.

**US-08 (MVP, FR-STAY-001 / FR-AIR-001 / FR-GROUND-001 / FR-XFER-001 / FR-RENT-001):** As a visitor I can request a stay or transport quote and know it is not confirmed. A successful request returns a reference and “request received; availability and price unconfirmed”; it must not create a paid order or issued ticket. Identity fields are minimized to what is necessary for a response. Future integrations require contracted provider evidence.

**US-09 (MVP, FR-SUP-001):** As a customer I can contact support about a booking. Given a case and my ownership, when I post a message, staff can respond and record the outcome; internal notes stay private. Notification failure queues a retry and does not silently resolve the case.

**US-10 (MVP, FR-I18N-001 / NFR-A11Y-001):** As a Persian reader using a keyboard I can complete the same task as an English reader. Given mixed English booking reference in Persian content, when displayed, then it remains readable and copied unchanged, direction is isolated and focus order follows the logical task. An error identifies the field and correction text; announcement does not rely on color. Switching language preserves the same record and safe route when translation exists; missing translation is labeled and never substitutes invented text.

**US-11 (MVP, FR-THEME-001 / FR-DATA-001):** As an agency administrator I can switch theme without losing booking records. Given active companion data, when theme changes on staging, then records remain retrievable with permissions, and no destructive uninstall occurs. With Woo absent, setup gives a clear dependency notice and storefront commerce does not appear operational.

On desktop use a main details column and secondary price/booking summary; on tablet place summary after description. At 200% zoom summary must not obscure content. **ASSUMPTION / ADR-001:** one WordPress installation serves one agency, with multiple scoped partner organizations; this is not a multi-agency SaaS design and does not assume Multisite. The reusable block theme and companion plugins are distributed and versioned separately. A customer, partner staff member or operator can hold multiple identities on one account. Physical merchandise, events, tour departures and cohorts are purchasable in MVP; stays, transport and rentals are manual requests only. Suppliers and gateway are independently contracted and have no assumed API. Crypto is off in every phase pending separate approval.

**WF-REG-001** creates a bounded hold under a short local transaction, then emits an outbox request for order processing. Payment verification occurs outside the transaction; booking confirmation waits for verified payment and agency confirmation. Unknown provider outcome enters reconciliation rather than a second charge. If a successful payment no longer has an allocated hold, create an exception/refund task. This is a distributed workflow with compensation, not a single cross-provider transaction.

Fictional 30-seat event: two customers race for seat 30; only the successful hold transaction is accepted. An order can be paid yet booking remains `paid_pending_confirmation`; a supplier reference or Woo order status alone does not confirm ticket issuance. Agency reviews exception with audit. **TC-REG-002** runs a concurrent last-seat test; **TC-PAY-001** repeats verified callback; **TC-AUTH-001** attempts another organization's export. All must pass before release.

**ADR-001/002 RECOMMENDATION:** deliver a reusable installable block theme ZIP plus separately installable versioned companion plugin ZIPs; one configured site is one agency. The theme supplies generic content and WooCommerce presentation, not durable reservations, gateway credentials, partner records or payment logic. Installing the theme must not automatically purchase a third-party plugin, transmit credentials or import fictional inventory. The agency companion is needed for travel workflows, not for rendering ordinary pages.

**TC-THEME-001:** activate with no Woo, with Woo only, and with companion; assert no fatal error, no false booking button and clear fallback. **TC-THEME-002:** switch themes with a booking/order and verify data survives and access control remains in companion. **TC-THEME-003:** change theme styles and a template, upgrade and verify user edits persist. **TC-THEME-004:** run keyboard, screen-reader, 200% zoom, RTL, long Persian title, price bidi and reduced-motion checks. **TC-THEME-005:** exercise Woo product, cart, Blocks checkout and supported classic checkout with HPOS configurations. Theme unit fixtures and an independent accessibility review are release gates.

**ADR-003 RECOMMENDATION:** ship one core companion with internal modules; split gateways and optional future integrations into separately installable adapters. The exact packaging is an open product decision. A module cannot infer authorization from a theme or UI. Core owns organization membership, audit, configuration, localization hooks, migrations and outbox; booking owns stock and hold lifecycle; catalog/tours/events/academy own content and domain rules; commerce translates domain offers to Woo products/order lines; payment adapter maps verified provider outcomes. Separate modules contain RFQ and other later-phase verticals. No component changes WordPress or Woo core.

**WF-PLUGIN-001:** application validates membership and request, opens short local transaction, updates owned rows and inserts an outbox event with a unique event ID. After commit, worker claims event, calls notification or provider using stable idempotency key where supported, records result and retries with bounded backoff. Never call provider while holding inventory locks. Timeout means unknown, so reconciliation precedes unsafe reattempt. Provider timestamps and signatures are validated by the actual contracted adapter, never guessed. See DOC-26 for envelope.

**TC-PLUGIN-001:** install, upgrade twice, interrupt and resume migration without duplicate effects. **TC-PLUGIN-002:** deactivate/reactivate around queued events, assert no duplicate notification or ledger mutation. **TC-PLUGIN-003:** Woo inactive or incompatible companion causes safe admin notice and no service order creation. **TC-PLUGIN-004:** theme switch preserves bookings and object authorization. **TC-PLUGIN-005:** simulate unknown network response and reconcile before reattempt. Automated integration tests run against each supported WP/Woo/PHP matrix combination; matrix remains VERIFY BEFORE BUILD.

Fictional occurrence O1 has capacity 30 and 29 allocated; hold H1 for one seat has `accepted_at_utc`, `expires_at_utc`, unique key and actor. Two simultaneous transactions compete for the final allocation; **TC-REG-002** requires one success and nonnegative capacity. **TC-DATA-001** checks unique membership and idempotency conflict; **TC-DATA-002** switches HPOS and uses Woo CRUD; **TC-DATA-003** verifies supplier cost omitted from public response; **TC-DATA-004** restores a backup and reconciles orders, booking, payment and outbox.

A WordPress site represents a single agency, not a multi-tenant hosting service. **ENT-USER** can be a shopper and a member of several **ENT-ORG** records through **ENT-MEMBER**. WordPress roles grant broad capabilities; they do not prove ownership of a particular partner resource. An active scoped membership and object relationship are checked on every relevant action. Public browse is allowed; MVP checkout requires sign-in. A traveler may differ from purchaser and has no automatic account access merely because they appear in booking.

**WF-AUTH-001:** authenticate user; validate request/nonce where applicable; identify current organization from membership, never trust client `org_id`; load target object and parent ownership; check status, scoped capability and purpose; filter fields; perform action; audit sensitive access and changes. On denial, return a consistent authorization response without revealing whether another organization’s record exists. Re-evaluate membership on asynchronous action execution. For approved agency impersonation/support, use time-limited scoped delegation with reason, actor, target, no ability to approve one's own elevated access, and immutable audit.

**TC-AUTH-001:** authenticated A member requests B's proposal, booking, export, media and search count; none disclose fields or record existence. **TC-AUTH-002:** customer changes order ID; object policy denies unrelated order. **TC-AUTH-003:** revoked membership cannot complete queued approval or reuse prior link. **TC-AUTH-004:** valid nonce without required capability or membership is denied. **TC-AUTH-005:** multilingual caches never serve confidential or another user's response. **TC-AUTH-006:** agency finance can issue authorized refund but cannot approve partner listing without that separate capability. Audit includes actor, object, purpose, time and outcome without PII payload.

MVP reserves manually managed local event occurrences, fixed-capacity tour departures and cohorts, never supplier inventory. `ENT-INVENTORY` capacity, `ENT-HOLD` and `ENT-BOOKING` are domain authority. Woo order state, gateway redirect, supplier status and booking state are independent. **NFR-CONC-001:** committed allocations cannot exceed capacity, including concurrent group requests and admin exceptions. Group quantity is all-or-nothing in MVP; never silently admit a partial party. Published visibility does not imply open registration, and an RFQ does not imply available stock.

**ADR-006:** ordinary public admission is accepted only when a local atomic hold is created with `registration_open_at <= server_now < registration_close_at`, user eligible, offer approved/published and capacity available. Use UTC instants and the configured IANA zone for display. The hold expiry and payment deadline are `min(accepted_at + 10 minutes, registration_close_at)`; there is no grace period or extension. At the deadline the hold is expired for new hold-related customer writes and payment initiation, even if the expiry worker has not released its allocation. Existing valid paid accepted booking may be confirmed after close; no new public admission after close.

**WF-REG-001:** (1) Authenticate, normalize request, validate input and idempotency key. (2) Begin a short database transaction, lock relevant inventory resource rows in deterministic order; read authoritative server time, offer revision and current eligibility. (3) If outside window, sold out, suspended or insufficient remaining capacity, roll back with a localized actionable error. Otherwise increment allocation, insert hold with expiry and record request-hash/idempotency result, commit. (4) Create/link Woo order through a separate idempotent process; a failure triggers safe compensating release or recoverable retry, never a remote call inside the lock. (5) Initiate payment through the approved adapter only before the deadline; do not allow a new hold-related customer write or new payment initiation at or after it. (6) Independently verify provider outcome outside the transaction and persist the authoritative local verification completion time; under local lock re-read hold state and verify amount/currency. Verification completed at or before the deadline may consume a still-allocated hold without provider paid_at; later verification additionally needs a trustworthy provider paid_at at or before the deadline. Otherwise record exception. If release already won, move expired booking to exception, preserve verified payment and do not reacquire inventory. (7) Agency confirms according to workflow and sends confirmation after commit.

**TC-REG-001:** check just before open, exactly open, just before close and exactly close using controlled server time. **TC-REG-002:** two parallel last-seat requests yield one success; assert allocation and count. **TC-REG-003:** verify locally at or before deadline without provider paid_at while allocation is unreleased; verify after deadline with trusted timely paid_at while unreleased; verify after deadline with missing/untrusted or late paid_at; and race verification against release. When release wins, assert `expired -> exception`, payment stays verified, allocation stays released, manual refund is queued and no oversell occurs. **TC-REG-004:** duplicate key same payload returns same result; changed payload conflicts. **TC-REG-005:** timezone offset changes, ambiguous local input and server/browser clock disagreement are handled explicitly. **TC-REG-006:** post-close waitlist and privileged exception enforce audit and capacity. **TC-REG-007:** provider timeout or stale inventory never produces confirmed ticket.

**ADR-007:** block physical/service mixtures and heterogeneous service inventory carts in MVP at add/update and server-side checkout validation. Same departure and offer may allow group quantity subject to all-or-nothing allocation. Show a localized explanation and offer separate checkout; avoid destroying the existing cart automatically. Logged-in account required. Revalidate cart compatibility, price version, hold allocation, amount and eligible gateway server-side. Each hold has deadline from DOC-24; no browser edit may extend it. Fresh stock snapshot must be checked transactionally rather than trusting catalog availability.

**TC-COM-001:** authenticated homogeneous service cart: create hold, calculate order and verify price/terms snapshot. **TC-COM-002:** attempt physical+event and two different departures through UI and Store API, plus classic endpoints only when classic support is declared; block consistently without discarding valid cart. **TC-COM-003:** expire hold before checkout/order payment and show recovery path. **TC-PAY-001:** duplicate callback produces one verified result and no double ledger event. **TC-COM-004:** simulate unknown gateway response, late paid/released hold and manual refund, reconciling order, payment and booking independently. **TC-COM-005:** tax, shipping and currency rounding match approved fixtures in Blocks and, when declared supported, classic checkout, and in declared HPOS modes. **TC-COM-006:** inaccessible or missing gateway shows useful message without fake confirmation.

| API-CAT-001 `GET /agency/v1/catalog` | Public filters: locale, offering type, destination, page; apply publication policy. | Public localized summaries, price with explicit currency and availability freshness. No confidential costs or partner contact. |

| API-BOOK-001 `POST /agency/v1/holds` | Signed-in user; idempotency key; offer ID/version, optional tier ID, quantity and participant eligibility references. Server resolves the occurrence, departure or cohort through the offer and determines time, org and capacity. | `201` hold ID, expiry/deadline and quote snapshot; transactional allocation; 409 closed/sold-out/changed quote. |

| API-BOOK-002 `GET /agency/v1/bookings/{id}` | Signed-in customer with object relationship or explicitly scoped authorized operator. | Filtered booking states, order reference, masked traveler fields and customer-safe terms. |

| API-PART-001 `POST /agency/v1/organizations/{id}/proposals` | Active membership and proposal-create capability for the named organization. Body: type, localized content, requested terms and draft revision. | Scoped draft ID/version; never auto-publish or expose net cost publicly. |

| API-PAY-001 `POST /agency/v1/payments/{adapter}/callback` | Provider-specific public callback with verified authentic origin/signature/inquiry as actual contract requires; browser/session nonce is not sufficient. | Acknowledge only per provider contract; enqueue/perform safe verification, deduplicate, persist evidence and trigger reconciliation. |

| API-TOUR-001 `POST /agency/v1/tours/{id}/versions` | Structured itinerary revision; returns version ID or validation/conflict. | MVP; active owning-org contributor or agency editor; no self-approval by default. |

| API-ACA-001 `POST /agency/v1/cohorts/{id}/enrollments` | Learner reference and accepted hold; validates eligibility, cohort and unique linkage; returns enrollment or conflict. | MVP; signed-in purchaser/authorized operator, not necessarily partner member. Capacity is allocated only through the shared hold transaction. |

| API-STAY-001 `POST /agency/v1/stay-requests` | Property, local check-in/out, occupancy and contact; returns request ID, never confirmed inventory. | MVP public RFQ; rate-limit and abuse-check submissions; protect subsequent access. |

| API-TICKET-001 `POST /agency/v1/ticket-requests` | Request details, passenger count and route; returns inquiry ID, no issuance. | MVP public inquiry with abuse controls; provider shopping/issuance P3 only. |

| API-RENT-001 `POST /agency/v1/rental-requests` | Dates, location, vehicle class and contact; returns request ID, no inventory promise. | MVP public RFQ; rate-limit and abuse-check submissions; protect subsequent access. |

| API-XFER-001 `POST /agency/v1/transfer-requests` | Pickup/drop-off, local date and time with IANA zone normalized to UTC, passenger and luggage counts, vehicle class, contact and idempotency key; returns unconfirmed request ID, never a booking, dispatch, payment or tracking promise. Invalid input returns 400/422; same key with conflicting request returns 409. | MVP public inquiry with rate limits and abuse controls; later access requires verified owner or authorized scoped organization. |
| API-MERCH-001 `POST /agency/v1/rfqs` | Requirements, supplier recipients and deadline; returns scoped draft. | P2 procurement; authorized agency staff and recipient-scoped partner access. |

| API-SUP-001 `POST /agency/v1/support-cases` | Bounded category, text and optional authorized object reference; returns case ID. | MVP; authenticated account; no access to another customer's object. |

| API-FIN-001 `POST /agency/v1/refunds/{id}/approve` | Expected revision, reason and idempotency key; returns approved case, not proof of provider refund. | MVP; separate finance approval capability and object policy. |
| API-CRYPTO-001 availability contract | Always returns unavailable; no address, payment instructions or activation function. | Investigation only, OFF; no actual provider endpoint. |

**TC-API-001:** reject malformed input, unauthorized object, stale version and duplicate conflicting request. **TC-API-002:** simultaneous holds cannot oversell; retry returns same ID. **TC-API-003:** public catalog and partner proposal responses never disclose another organization's data. **TC-API-004:** replay provider callback and event delivery; payment and ledger effect occur once. **TC-API-005:** timeout then late provider success creates unknown/reconciled state; no invented confirmed ticket. **TC-API-006:** verify rate limit, localized validation, schema compatibility and privacy-safe correlation IDs. Test both Blocks/Store API extension and classic integration where supported.

**TC-SEC-001:** user A probes user B/partner records through REST, export, file, search and cache; no sensitive fields leak. **TC-SEC-002:** valid CSRF nonce without object capability fails. **TC-SEC-003:** forged and replayed provider callback cannot confirm or double-credit. **TC-SEC-004:** malicious upload, SQL/XSS input and SSRF targets are rejected in all surfaces. **TC-SEC-005:** secrets, passport-like values and card data absent from logs/notifications. **TC-SEC-006:** execute revoked-access and backup restore scenarios, then independent penetration and privacy review before production data.

**ADR-016 RECOMMENDATION, unmeasured:** propose 99.5% monthly availability for the public catalog, and a 15-minute scheduler lag alert threshold for initial planning; business must approve stricter/appropriate targets after measurement. Time-critical hold expiry cannot depend on that broad 15-minute operational threshold; define a separate tighter worker cadence and overdue hold alert after feasibility tests. No SLO implies guaranteed payment/provider uptime. Define eligible-service success and exclusions before measuring.

Fictional test: scheduler is stopped for 12 minutes while an event closes. New holds fail at close based on server time; delayed expiry processes once after scheduler resumes; a verified payment whose allocation was released enters manual exception. **TC-OPS-001:** stop/restart worker and verify no oversell or duplicate delivery. **TC-OPS-002:** interrupt migration and safely resume. **TC-OPS-003:** restore backup and reconcile external payment events after recovery. **TC-OPS-004:** deploy incompatible adapter to staging and confirm dependency warning/no service checkout. **TC-OPS-005:** trigger queue alert and use runbook to resolve with audit. **TC-OPS-006:** exercise theme and plugin artifact rollback with preserved orders.

**Status:** DRAFT specification; review pending. **Purpose:** define structured, reviewed tour departures and operational delivery. **Prepared from perspectives:** tour operations, partner, booking, UX and privacy. **Accountable reviewer:** tour operations lead. **Dependencies:** [DOC-22](DOC-22_DATA-MODEL-ERD-DICTIONARY.md), [DOC-24](DOC-24_BOOKING-INVENTORY-REGISTRATION.md), [DOC-36](DOC-36_PARTNER-PORTALS-CONTRACTS.md). **Decision:** MVP is locally allocated, fixed-capacity, manually confirmed departures; live supplier booking is later and conditional on contract (ADR-012).

**FR-TOUR-001:** an approved leader may create many tour definitions and dated departures, for one or many destinations. A traveler can inspect inclusions and reserve an available departure; agency staff approve content and confirm bookings. Site-wide capability alone never authorizes another organization's records (NFR-SEC-001).
| ENT-TOUR | organization, localized title/description, languages, age and group limits, fitness, accessibility, required documents, cancellation terms, version, approval state |
| ENT-DEPARTURE | tour version, start/end with IANA zones, capacity, currency, price snapshot, owner, publication and operation states |
| ENT-STOP | ordered city/country, coordinates optional, arrival/departure instant plus zone, meeting point, overnight, contingency |
| ENT-LEG | origin/destination stops, transport type, provider reference if known, planned instants/zones, luggage, connection buffer, allocation; private net cost |
| ENT-ITINERARY | day, ordered timed activity, type, description, inclusions, meal and equipment; lodging night, room allocation, occupancy and booking status |

**WF-TOUR-001:** leader drafts → submits immutable version → agency reviews → approves or returns with reasons → schedules departure → publishes → customer selects quantity → signs in → atomic local hold → checkout → verified payment → agency confirms → fulfillment. Capacity and payment follow [DOC-24](DOC-24_BOOKING-INVENTORY-REGISTRATION.md); Woo order is not confirmation. Hold expiry is at most ten minutes and never later than applicable cutoff. Independently verified payment completed locally by the deadline can consume a still-allocated hold without provider paid_at. After the deadline, require trustworthy provider paid_at at or before the deadline and a still-unreleased allocation; if already released, booking transitions `expired → exception` with prior expiry retained in audit, allocation remains released and payment remains verified; route to manual refund review with no new admission or automatic reclaim. Public pages show unavailable or request-only if no active departure.

**UI-TOUR-001** builder has identity, stops, leg, day, lodging/meal/equipment, cost and review panels; reorder controls work with keyboard and announce validation. **UI-TOUR-002** departure details show route, local times, price, inclusions, exclusions, terms and capacity state. **API-TOUR-001** proposed `POST /agency/v1/tours/{id}/versions` accepts revision and structured arrays, checks membership, validates server-side, and returns 201 revision ID or 403/409/422. All mutations audit actor, organization and version; the public endpoint excludes confidential costs. Staff cannot approve their own proposal unless governance explicitly permits it.

**TC-TOUR-001:** create three stops with zones and detect leg inversion; **TC-TOUR-002:** customer response omits net costs; **TC-REG-002:** parallel last-seat requests yield one hold; **TC-AUTH-001:** cross-organization access denied. Test editing a published schedule, inaccessible service, missed connection, partial group and supplier withdrawal. **OPEN DECISION:** operations lead must determine approval, document and change-notice policies; finance must approve markup/tax and handling of group partials. Supplier agreements and legal terms are dependencies, not assumed. Analytics use aggregate searches, holds, paid-pending-confirmation and confirmation with no traveler identifiers in analytics.

**FR-EVT-001:** a reusable ENT-EVENT describes localized program, eligibility, terms and venue; each ENT-OCCURRENCE is independently scheduled and stores UTC instants plus named IANA zone, visibility start/end, registration open and close, capacity, tiers, price/tax snapshot, payment deadline policy, sessions, optional meal/transport, waiver version and waitlist policy. Validate open < close ≤ event start unless an agency exception is approved; unpublished drafts never accept public registration. Distinguish visible-not-open, open, sold-out, closed, suspended, canceled and rescheduled. Sessions have independent capacity when enabled; no overselling event or session inventory.

**WF-REG-001:** ordinary admission occurs atomically at hold creation only for `open_at <= server_now < close_at`, eligibility and capacity. Hold TTL = min(10 minutes, close minus now); payment deadline is hold expiry. Independent payment verification completed locally at or before the deadline may consume a still-allocated hold without provider `paid_at`. After the deadline, require trustworthy provider `paid_at` at or before the deadline and a still-unreleased allocation. If the hold was released, booking transitions `expired → exception` with prior expiry retained in audit; allocation remains released and payment remains verified. Route to manual refund review with no new admission or automatic reclaim. If trustworthy payment time is unavailable after deadline, manual exception. An authorized admin may grant an explicit post-close exception with reason, actor and audit; capacity still applies. Waitlist invitations never override closure. Booking, order, payment and event status remain distinct.

**UI-EVT-001** occurrence detail exposes zone, dates, price, availability, age, venue accessibility, program, gear, waiver, optional services and clear registration state. **UI-EVT-002** registration asks purchaser, attendee, guardian if needed, dietary options, transport and agreement. Only necessary dietary details are retained with restricted access and defined retention. **API-BOOK-001** proposed `POST /agency/v1/holds` accepts offer ID/version, optional tier ID, quantity, participant eligibility references and an idempotency key. The server resolves the occurrence from the selected offer; the client does not submit a second authoritative occurrence ID. The response includes hold ID, expiry and price snapshot, or 409 for cutoff/capacity. Server time and atomic inventory rule govern, regardless of UI state. Partner may propose owned event; agency reviews; assigned check-in staff can see only needed attendee list and mark attendance, not payment instruments. Notification and audit events cover publication, hold, payment, confirmation, change and cancellation.

**TC-REG-001:** open−1ms fails, open succeeds, close−1ms succeeds only if hold can be created, close fails; verify TTL and UTC conversion. **TC-REG-002:** parallel attempts on final seat admit one. **TC-EVT-001:** locally verified on-time payment needs no provider timestamp; after-deadline verification requires trusted on-time provider timestamp and unreleased allocation, and released hold yields booking `expired → exception`, prior expiry audited, allocation released and payment verified without new admission; **TC-EVT-002:** session and event capacities both enforced. Test duplicate callbacks, waitlist exception, attendee list authorization, dietary data redaction, reduced motion and mixed scripts. KPI aggregates: published-to-view, view-to-hold, hold-to-paid, no-show and refund rates; do not send sensitive fields to analytics. **OPEN DECISION:** owner must set waitlist, cancellation and guardian rules; venue contracts and qualified local legal review remain dependencies. Accept only after a production-like time/race test and operator signoff.

**FR-ACA-001:** ENT-COURSE is a reusable syllabus with localized outcomes, prerequisites and version. ENT-COHORT is a scheduled delivery with city/venue, instructor assignments, session instants and IANA zones, registration window, capacity, tuition, accessibility and policies. ENT-ENROLLMENT binds one learner and cohort with eligibility evidence, hold, booking, attendance and completion status; a payer may differ from learner. ENT-CERTIFICATE has opaque verification reference, version, issuer, issue/revocation status, never an easily enumerable public student record. Materials remain accessible to authorized enrolled learners after admission closes under the published access policy.

**WF-ACA-001:** coordinator proposes course and cohort → agency approves → visibility/public admission → eligibility review → atomic hold → payment verified → manual confirmation → attendance → phase-2 assessment → completion → conditional certificate issuance. Each cohort independently uses WF-REG-001 in DOC-30: open inclusive, close exclusive, TTL min(10 minutes, time remaining), payment deadline equals hold expiry, and independent verification completed locally at or before that deadline may consume a still-allocated hold without provider `paid_at`. After the deadline, trustworthy provider `paid_at` at or before the deadline and a still-unreleased allocation are both required. If released, booking transitions `expired → exception` with prior expiry retained in audit; allocation remains released and payment remains verified. Route to manual refund review without new admission or automatic reclaim. A post-close exception requires authorized staff, reason and capacity check. No certificate implies accreditation unless verified.

**UI-ACA-001** course page lists cohorts and each independent state; **UI-ACA-002** learner form collects identity and only necessary prerequisites/guardian details; **UI-ACA-003** instructor roster and attendance; phase-2 reviewer enters assessment and certificate decision. **API-ACA-001** proposed `POST /agency/v1/cohorts/{id}/enrollments` validates the authenticated purchaser/learner relationship and applicable operator organization membership, prerequisites, cohort and an existing accepted hold in a transaction. Capacity is allocated only by the shared hold transaction; enrollment references that hold and never allocates a second seat. Retry is idempotent. Instructor sees only assigned cohorts and minimum roster; agency reviewer approves; learner sees own result. Prevent instructor or room overlapping sessions by interval checks, with an explicit reviewed exception. Store evidence securely and apply retention policy; aggregate funnel and attendance metrics only.

**TC-ACA-001** simultaneously render A closed/B open and reject closed server-side; **TC-REG-001** exact open/close and time-zone rules; **TC-ACA-002** no certificate when required attendance or assessment absent; **TC-AUTH-001** instructor from another organization cannot read roster. Test edits to schedules, waitlist after close, payment races, accessible venue information and materials after cutoff. Notifications: cohort changes to enrolled learner and assigned instructor; sensitive assessment only via authenticated portal. **OPEN DECISION:** director to approve prerequisite evidence, attendance thresholds, assessment appeals, certificate content, verification disclosure and material retention; instructor, venue and legal contracts not evidenced.

**FR-STAY-001:** an ENT-PROPERTY belongs to a partner organization and includes localized address, zone, description, facilities, access constraints and review evidence. ENT-UNITTYPE includes occupancy, capacity, amenities; ENT-UNIT identifies an individually blocked unit or villa. ENT-RATE defines period, eligible occupancy, meal plan, currency, taxes, refundable terms, price and expiry. ENT-INVENTORY counts local room-type inventory per night, while individually unique villas use overlapping-interval exclusion. ENT-QUOTE stores requested dates, guests, price components, expiry, supplier approval and version. Supplier net rate and rooming list are restricted. Local date is property zone; checkout date is exclusive.

**WF-STAY-001:** property submits proposal → agency reviews → publishes factual listing → customer requests quote → supplier and agency verify inventory/terms → agency communicates offer. MVP ends at request/quote: booking is manual offline if separately arranged and not represented as confirmed on this platform. In phase 2, only after contracts and tests, reserve every requested night atomically in one local transaction, with a unique inventory lock order to prevent deadlocks; rollback all nights if any unavailable. External inventory and local locks cannot share a transaction; recheck with supplier, reconcile and compensate via outbox. Booking confirmation is separate from payment and supplier acceptance. Holds and late payment follow DOC-24.

**UI-STAY-001** property and date search shows freshness and “Request a quote” / «درخواست قیمت» for MVP; **UI-STAY-002** partner form captures room types, policy, rates and accessible features. **API-STAY-001** proposed `POST /agency/v1/stay-requests` accepts property, local check-in/out, occupancy, contact and idempotency key; validates checkout > check-in, date range, ownership and consent, returning request ID, not availability. Partner reads only owned property and assigned requests; customer reads own; agency approves changes. Store rooming data only when needed and limit access; audit exports and retention. Aggregate requests, quotes and confirmed stays without names in analytics.

**TC-STAY-001** overlapping three-night capacity and atomic rollback; **TC-STAY-002** unique villa collision; **TC-STAY-003** payment/supplier failure reconciliation; **TC-AUTH-001** partner cannot read another property's rooming list. Include daylight-saving transitions, rate expiry, policy changes after purchase and accessible accommodation accuracy. **OPEN DECISION:** operator to establish merchant role, cancellation windows, allotment rights, no-show, tax and accommodation compliance; supplier agreements and retention review are prerequisites for phase 2. No provider endpoint or live property inventory is asserted.

**FR-AIR-001 / FR-GROUND-001:** collect routes, departure/arrival location, local dates/time zones, traveler count, fare class, baggage and accessibility needs in an inquiry. ENT-QUOTE holds source, retrieved time, expiry, currency, fare components, terms and freshness; ENT-TRAVELER contains necessary identity matched to ticketing rules; ENT-BOOKING holds local state; ENT-TICKET holds issuer reference and issuance status separately from ENT-ORDER and ENT-PAYMENT. Supplier reservation locator, passenger information and travel documents are restricted. Retain only documented necessary identity fields and apply deletion/legal hold policy.

**WF-TICKET-001 (future integration):** search supplier → show tentative quote and restrictions → reprice/recheck → acquire supplier hold if actually supported → collect verified payment → request issuance → inspect authoritative issuance result → confirm ticket or open exception. Supplier state, payment verification, Woo order and fulfillment remain independent. A redirect or successful order cannot prove issuance. No DB transaction spans a supplier call: persist request and outbox, use idempotency where supplier supports it, handle ambiguous timeouts by inquiry/reconciliation rather than blindly creating a second reservation. Supplier-specific seat maps, refunds, PNR and revalidation are available only where contract and capability evidence support them. Customer changes and disruption notices enter support queue; not all supplier changes are self-service.

**UI-TICKET-001** displays request-only notice in MVP: “Availability must be confirmed” / «موجودی باید تأیید شود». Future results show freshness, price expiry, carrier/operator, all fees, baggage, change/refund conditions and names required. **API-TICKET-001** proposed `POST /agency/v1/ticket-requests` creates inquiry; future adapter contracts expose abstract search/quote/reservation/issuance/status/cancel semantics, with actual mapping unresolved. Public calls cannot enumerate another customer’s references. Assigned ticketing staff see passenger data only for service delivery; user sees their own request, finance sees amounts but not documents. Never log identity documents or secrets.

section: 2. Fictional scenario F — payment succeeds, flight issuance fails
source_text: Proposed/mock integration only; no licensed or live supplier exists. User searches Tehran–destination, one adult, receives illustrative fare 50,000,000 IRR, expires in five minutes; fare, tax and baggage terms appear. Customer signs in, reviews passenger name and accepts restrictions. Future contracted supplier confirms a reservation/hold; payment is independently verified for 50,000,000 IRR and Woo order is paid. Issuance request times out, then a provider status check returns failure. Booking remains `exception`, not confirmed; ENT-TICKET is not issued; outbox raises an operations task and customer sees “Payment received; ticket not yet issued” / «پرداخت دریافت شد؛ بلیت هنوز صادر نشده است». Assigned agent checks authoritative status, tells customer, requests consent for an alternative or approves refund under contract; finance submits and reconciles refund separately. Notification contains no passport number. The reservation and issue methods are hypothetical abstractions and require actual provider mapping, not asserted APIs.

**TC-TICKET-001:** paid order with failed issuance never appears as ticket issued; **TC-TICKET-002:** ambiguous timeout does not issue twice; **TC-TICKET-003:** stale fare requires fresh acceptance; **TC-AUTH-001:** other organization cannot retrieve traveler data. Test rail/bus operators with no seat maps, station time-zone changes, supplier downtime, partial group issue, duplicate webhook and reconciliation. Aggregate search-to-request, issue-failure and time-to-resolution without identity in analytics. **OPEN DECISION:** ticketing lead must secure credentials, sandbox, availability and fare contracts, dispute and refund rights, support SLA, licensing and production certification; none are confirmed. Acceptance requires realistic supplier contract tests before enabling a route.

**FR-XFER-001:** transfer inquiry includes pickup/drop-off location and zoned time, passengers, luggage, accessibility, vehicle class and flight reference optional. Dispatcher assigns an eligible vehicle and driver only after agency review; waiting fees, cancellation and tracking require explicit terms and verified technical/legal basis. **FR-RENT-001:** ENT-VEHICLE records organization, category (bicycle, motorcycle, car, van), availability intervals, capacity, license class, insurance status and maintenance block; ENT-RENTAL records local pickup/drop-off instants, renter, required driver eligibility, quote, deposit terms, fuel/mileage policy and signed condition records. Avoid retaining images or licenses longer than approved policy; never ask for raw payment card data.

**WF-RENT-001:** request → agency/supplier quote → customer agrees → (phase 2) interval hold and payment where contracted → manual confirmation → identity/license check → pickup inspection → return inspection → settle approved fees/deposit → close or dispute. Prevent overlapping rental, transfer and maintenance intervals for the same vehicle; acquire ordered locks, validate interval `[start,end)` and keep buffer for inspection. Deposit authorization versus actual charge is provider-specific and unverified; do not represent an authorization as captured or promise it exists. No automatic payout. **UI-RENT-001** quote request displays inclusions, coverage exclusions, required documents and “Request only” / «فقط درخواست قیمت»; UI-RENT-002 pickup/return checklist supports photos subject to consent and access. **API-RENT-001** proposed `POST /agency/v1/rental-requests` stores dates, vehicle class and contact, returning request ID. Partner sees own vehicles and assigned request; renter sees own record; finance sees monetary details; admin approval is required for publication and material changes.

**UI-XFER-001** is a dedicated chauffeured-transfer request form using the accessible RFQ pattern. It collects pickup and drop-off locations and local date/time with named IANA zone, passenger and luggage counts, vehicle class, contact information, accessibility needs and optional flight reference. It explains that an agency will seek a driver; it shows no driver assignment, live dispatch, tracking or payment in MVP. A requester may submit an inquiry under public RFQ abuse controls; subsequent request access requires verified identity and ownership. Agency staff and an explicitly assigned operator have scoped access; other partners do not.

**API-XFER-001** proposed `POST /agency/v1/transfer-requests` accepts those fields and an idempotency key and returns an unconfirmed request ID, never a booking or availability guarantee. Server validation requires bounded nonempty locations and contact, integer passengers greater than zero, a nonnegative luggage count, an allowed vehicle class, valid local instants and recognized IANA zones. Convert each local time using its stated zone, reject nonexistent or ambiguous local times without explicit resolution, and require drop-off after pickup. Reject malformed or conflicting idempotency retries; apply rate limits and abuse controls without revealing other requests. No provider endpoint, payment, live dispatch or tracking capability is assumed.

**TC-RENT-001** interval collision including maintenance and buffer; **TC-RENT-002** expired license prevents handover; **TC-RENT-003** damage dispute does not automatically charge; **TC-XFER-001** transfer uses driver assignment, not renter license rules. **TC-XFER-002** submit a valid request and verify the response contains an unconfirmed request ID, not a booking; reject invalid time zones, reversed instants, nonpositive passengers and conflicting idempotency retries, enforce abuse limits and deny access to another owner. Test tax, daylight saving, missed pickup, device-offline checklists and unauthorized partner access. Aggregate inquiry-to-quote, rental utilization and dispute counts without location trails. **OPEN DECISION:** operations/legal must approve coverage, licensing, security deposit, provider capabilities, fee disputes, safety escalation and document retention. No live tracking is assumed.

**FR-MERCH-001:** ENT-MERCH is a Woo product/variation, with SKU, localized description, dimensions, weight, tax/shipping class, stock, price and return terms. ENT-RFQ stores buyer, specifications, quantity, delivery deadline, permitted recipients, version and due date; ENT-QUOTE stores supplier unit price, production lead time, setup, shipping, tax and expiry. ENT-PRODUCTION stores selected supplier, approved sample version, milestones, quality checks, shipment and invoice references; confidential artwork is access-controlled and scan-checked. Define intellectual-property permission and retention before production.

**WF-MERCH-001:** agency publishes product → customer signs in and buys physical goods in a physical-only cart → verified payment → pick/pack/ship → customer support. Supplier manufacturing path in phase 2: agency creates RFQ → suppliers submit private bids → agency compares → selects supplier → reviews sample → authorizes production → inspects → receives invoice → finance records payable and manually settles after approval. Quote is not a purchase order; production cannot begin merely because RFQ is sent. Woo order, production, shipment, refund and payout are independent. Use Woo APIs for product and order access; do not assume vendor marketplace or automatic payment splitting.

**UI-MERCH-001** product page shows variants, total, shipping policy and accurate stock. **UI-MERCH-002** private RFQ form includes artwork version, dimensions, material, quantity, destination, due date, proof and inspection requirements. **API-MERCH-001** proposed `POST /agency/v1/rfqs` accepts scoped suppliers, deadline and requirements; returns draft ID; submitting creates audit and notifications. Organization membership gates bids and files; a maker cannot see competitors’ bids. Downloads are authorized per object, filenames sanitized and content scanned; no public art URLs by default. Analytics tracks aggregate conversion, late production and defect rates.

**TC-MERCH-001** physical-only cart checks shipping and refuses service item; **TC-MERCH-002** another maker cannot see bids/art; **TC-MERCH-003** no production authorization until sample approved; **TC-MERCH-004** failed inspection blocks payable approval. Test stock races, variants, refunds, file expiry, return exceptions and multilingual product data. **OPEN DECISION:** procurement owner must approve IP, order cancellation, minimum quantities, quality tolerance, shipping terms and payout evidence. Supplier availability and extension compatibility remain unverified.

**FR-PART-001:** ENT-ORG holds legal/display name, partner types, contact, review and suspension states; ENT-MEMBER associates a user to an organization with status, role and effective dates. A user may belong to several organizations; all resource access uses explicit organization context and object ownership, not only a global role. ENT-CONTRACT holds parties, version, effective period, approved services, commission basis, cancellation terms, signed evidence location and confidentiality flags. ENT-RFQ and ENT-QUOTE have recipient lists and independent approval/version/expiry. Verification/KYB requirements are determined by qualified reviewers, not assumed complete.

**WF-PART-001:** applicant enters organization and contact → uploads minimal requested evidence → agency performs recorded review → approves or requests changes → partner accepts proposed contract → scoped staff create a listing proposal → agency reviews and publishes. Manual RFQ in phase 2 selects recipients, captures quote deadlines, supports confidential responses and approval; no supplier commitment is inferred until signed purchase terms. **UI-PART-001** onboarding has clear draft/submitted/suspended states; **UI-PART-002** partner dashboard shows own proposals, assignments and permitted earnings with accessible tables. Notification: “Your proposal is under review” / «پیشنهاد شما در حال بررسی است».

**API-PART-001** proposed `POST /agency/v1/organizations/{org_id}/proposals` checks logged-in identity, active membership, capability, ownership, CSRF protection where applicable and schema; return 201 proposal ID, 403 denied, 409 stale revision. A nonce is not authorization: WordPress says nonces are not authentication or access control ([official guidance](https://developer.wordpress.org/apis/security/nonces/), retrieved 2026-11-17).
